subject: Discovery recap: streaming UX knobs & p95/concurrency qualification with Finlytics
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@finlytics.ai>, Aisha Collins <aisha.collins@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 20:28:00 -0400
Subject: Discovery recap: streaming UX knobs & p95/concurrency qualification with Finlytics

Thanks again for the time today — useful conversation. Below is a concise recap so we have a shared set of goals and immediate next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of needs we heard
- Product: real-time transcription + light semantic extraction for customer support (speaker diarization, per-utterance metadata).
- SLO goal: p95 end-to-end streaming token latency <= 250ms for short responses (<= 32 tokens) during steady-state; allow 2x higher for long tail but want predictable degradation.
- Concurrency: 350 sustained concurrent users during business hours with bursts to ~1,200 for short windows (5–8 minutes).
- Pain points: current self-hosted Triton setup has frequent p95 spikes during cold-starts and when KV caches miss; client-side SDK doesn’t handle partials well (UX flicker).
- Current stack: Finlytics runs on GCP (us-east4) with Triton-backed endpoints, custom multiplexer, and a thin websocket layer in front.

Success criteria for a PoC
1) Reproduce Finlytics load profile in our test harness with synthetic speaker-turns.
2) Demonstrate stable p95 <= 250ms for 90% of test windows at 350 concurrency and controlled bursts to 1,200.
3) Show streaming UX improvements via our partials + flush knobs (reduce perceived first-token latency).
4) Provide concrete operational knobs (batch size, prefill KV, warm pools) and an estimated cost delta.

Immediate next steps (owners + dates)
- Tessa: share Redwood MOP draft and test harness link by Mon 5/10 (attached).
- Marissa: collect a 1-hour perf trace from Finlytics (server logs + client-side timing) — Samir to share by Tue 5/11.
- Ben: propose a PoC SOW and cost outline by Fri 5/14.
- Samir/Aisha: confirm procurement timeline and PoC decision maker (legal/IT) by Tue 5/11.

Notes / open questions
- Are there internal rate limits or routing rules that will block sustained bursts from single IP ranges?
- Will Finlytics be able to run a small agent to collect kv-cache hit metrics (Marissa provided the script link in call)?

Attachments: redwood_mop_draft.pdf (draft MOP), example test harness link below.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCxyz-redwood-mop-draft

Thanks — looking forward to the perf logs.

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
https://www.redwood.com

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: streaming UX knobs & p95/concurrency qualification with Finlytics

Thanks Tessa — this captures it. A few clarifications from our side:

- The SDK "flicker" is most visible for mobile clients when the first partial comes in late; perceived latency is what users complain about. We do not need 250ms for 512-token summaries, just for the initial partials / short responses.
- Procurement: we have a procurement cycle that expects a PoC approval within 6 weeks if technical shows are green. Legal will want a short security questionnaire answered (SOC2 scope).
- Tech contact: I can get the perf trace; Aisha will coordinate with ops for access (we may have to scrub PII).

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood provide a suggested warm-pool sizing based on the numbers above (350 sustained, 1,200 bursts)?
2) Do you have a short checklist for SOC2 artifacts we should expect during PoC?

I'll share logs by Tue 5/11 EOD. If we can lock a short technical readout next Wed 5/12, that would be ideal.

Samir

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: streaming UX knobs & p95/concurrency qualification with Finlytics

Thanks for the notes — looping in a quick technical sketch while we wait for the trace. Attaching a small perf bundle (finlytics_perf_logs.tar.gz) when you send the trace — please include: client-side timestamps (first-byte, first-partial), server recv time, KV cache hit flags, and batch sizes.

Initial technical observations and hypotheses
- Likely causes of p95 spikes:
  * KV cache cold misses on long-tail speaker-turns (cold prefixes) cause backend generation to go from cached KV path to full decode path — big latency delta.
  * Suboptimal batching: current multiplexer uses fixed windowing; for streaming use-cases, adaptive batching with max-latency cutoffs helps maintain first-token latency while still improving throughput.
  * Model variant fallbacks: if current Triton variant is overloaded, some requests hit a heavier quantized path that increases p95.

Suggested PoC knobs to try (we can run these in our harness)
- Maintain a small warm pool per shard (size = ceil(350 / number_of_shards) + 20% overhead).
- Prefill KV for common prefixes observed in logs during business hours.
- Adaptive batching: target batch windows of 8–12ms for short partials; allow larger batches for long-form decode.
- Backpressure: client-side token pacing + websocket keepalive to avoid head-of-line blocking.

What we'll attach when you send logs
- A short annotated trace (HTML) with KV-hit overlays and per-request batch sizes.
- A baseline report that simulates steady-state 350 concurrency profile and 5-minute bursts to 1,200.

Follow-ups
- Samir/Aisha: send logs by Tue 5/11.
- Tessa: I'll finalize the MOP and drop a PoC SOW draft for Ben to price by Fri 5/14.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
